subject: Archaeology
title: Mesa Verde's Cliff Dwellings
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mesa Verde's Cliff Dwellings.

hook.text: In 1888, two cowboys chasing stray cattle looked across a canyon and saw an entire city built into a cliff.

buildup.text: The Ancestral Puebloans built over 600 cliff dwellings in Mesa Verde, Colorado, around 1200 CE.

discovery.text: Cliff Palace alone had 150 rooms and 23 kivas — underground ceremonial chambers carved into rock.

twist.text: Within a century of building them, the Puebloans abandoned every dwelling. Drought drove them away.

climax.text: Their descendants — the Hopi and Pueblo peoples — still live in the American Southwest today.

punchline.text: They left their cliff homes but never left the region.

quiz.question: Why did the Ancestral Puebloans abandon their Mesa Verde cliff dwellings?
options: Enemy attacks forced them to flee south
Severe drought made the area uninhabitable
Volcanic eruptions destroyed the water supply

details.summary: Mesa Verde in Colorado contains over 600 cliff dwellings built by Ancestral Puebloans in sandstone alcoves between 1190 and 1300 CE. The largest, Cliff Palace, has 150 rooms. These dwellings were used for only about a century before being abandoned during a prolonged drought.
details.whyItMatters: Mesa Verde's cliff dwellings represent one of North America's most dramatic architectural achievements. Their brief occupation and sudden abandonment illustrate how climatic stress can force entire communities to relocate.
takeaways: Over 600 cliff dwellings built in sandstone alcoves from 1190-1300 CE
Cliff Palace is the largest with 150 rooms and 23 kivas
Abandoned during a severe drought in the late 13th century

faq.question: Why did the Ancestral Puebloans build in cliff alcoves?
faq.answer: The alcoves provided natural shelter from rain and snow while offering defensive advantages. The south-facing orientation captured winter sun for warmth while the overhang shaded summer heat. Natural springs in the sandstone provided water. The locations combine practical and defensive benefits.

faq.question: Where did the cliff dwellers go when they left?
faq.answer: Tree-ring data shows a severe drought from 1276 to 1299. Communities migrated south to the Rio Grande and Little Colorado River areas with more reliable water. Modern Pueblo peoples in New Mexico and Arizona are their direct descendants and maintain cultural connections to Mesa Verde.
